Investigators are now shifting their focus toward finding the root cause of what the company formally characterized as an "anomaly." Jeff Bezos addressed the incident on social media, acknowledging a "very rough day" but reiterating the company’s resilience, stating it will rebuild whatever is necessary and return to flying.
The timing of the failure is particularly challenging for Blue Origin. Just days prior, NASA had awarded the company a high-stakes contract to launch the first of three uncrewed missions later this year, intended to kickstart construction on a $20 billion lunar base. The New Glenn rocket is a critical pillar of NASA’s broader Artemis program, meant to launch the heavy lunar landers that will ferry astronauts to the moon.
NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman emphasized that spaceflight is uniquely unforgiving and that building heavy-lift infrastructure presents immense technical hurdles. He stated that the space agency would closely support the upcoming investigation to fully evaluate the near-term impacts on the Artemis schedule. sources.news_title: Jeff Bezos' New Glenn Rocket Destroyed on the Launchpad at Cape Canaveral in One of the Largest Rocket Explosions in U.S. History
sources.text:
A 321-foot rocket fully loaded with propellant detonated on its launchpad at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on the night of 28 May 2026, lighting up the Florida coast with an orange fireball visible from Cocoa Beach and shaking the walls of homes across Brevard County.
Here's our video of the explosion at Launch Complex 36. It happened about 9 pm ET (0100 UTC) as Blue Origin was beginning a static fire test of its New Glenn rocket.
Watch live views: https://t.co/tm2wZQmAVD pic.twitter.com/PmbgQC6Qmq
— Spaceflight Now (@SpaceflightNow) May 29, 2026
Blue Origin was conducting a static fire test, meaning the rocket’s engines are ignited at full power while the vehicle remains clamped to the launchpad, a standard pre-flight check designed to confirm engine performance before committing to a launch date. A static fire does not involve launch; the rocket stays bolted to the ground and burns fuel at full thrust for a controlled number of seconds while the test team monitors pressure, temperature, and combustion data in real time. Because New Glenn was almost certainly fully fuelled for the procedure, what detonated at Launch Complex 36 was among the largest rocket explosions ever recorded on American soil. No personnel were hurt, Cape Canaveral Space Force Station confirmed, and the resulting fire was allowed to burn itself out under the watch of emergency crews who remained on scene for more than an hour after the blast.
The booster that exploded was named “No, It’s Necessary,” and it was a brand new vehicle, not a previously flown unit. The explosion occurred just before the static fire could be completed, and it was not clear how far into the ignition sequence the test had progressed before the detonation. The fireball sent debris raining down across the complex, and at least one of LC-36’s lightning protection towers, the tall steel structures that ring a launchpad to intercept lightning strikes and protect the vehicle during fuelling and testing, was seen collapsing in footage captured by witnesses. Several hangars, buildings, and test facilities are situated around the LC-36 complex, and the full extent of structural damage to the pad infrastructure had not been assessed as of early Friday morning.
The vehicle was being prepared for its fourth orbital mission, designated NG-4, which was set to carry 48 internet satellites into orbit for Amazon’s Leo broadband constellation, the company’s planned competitor to SpaceX’s Starlink network. Amazon had contracted Blue Origin for 24 launches in total, and NG-4 was to be the first delivery under that agreement. On the day before the explosion, Amazon published statements touting its reliance on Blue Origin and describing New Glenn as a “reusable, heavy-lift rocket.” No Leo satellites were physically aboard for Thursday’s static fire test, Amazon confirmed, meaning the payload loss was zero. The rocket itself, worth hundreds of millions of dollars, was not so fortunate.
Blue Origin's New Glenn just blew up at LC-36 while attempting to Static Fire ahead of NG-4.https://t.co/tANS0dWyIH pic.twitter.com/PztxFoBqIw
— NSF – NASASpaceflight.com (@NASASpaceflight) May 29, 2026
New Glenn had only recently been cleared to fly again following its third mission on 19 April 2026, during which the rocket’s second stage suffered a malfunction and failed to reach its target orbit. A cryogenic leak froze a hydraulic line during the second-stage engine burn, causing a loss of thrust that stranded AST SpaceMobile’s BlueBird 7 satellite in an orbit too low to be usable. Cryogenic propellants, the super-cold liquid oxygen and liquid hydrogen that power large rockets, are stored at temperatures as low as minus 253 degrees Celsius; even a small leak in a pressurised line can cause surrounding components to seize solid in seconds, locking the valves and actuators that control engine thrust. The satellite could not be recovered and re-entered the atmosphere, burning up entirely. The FAA grounded New Glenn and required a full investigation; Blue Origin identified nine corrective actions, and the agency verified their implementation before clearing the rocket to return to flight.
That clearance came through just days before Thursday’s explosion. Blue Origin’s chief executive Dave Limp posted a video just hours before the blast showing a new vehicle being installed on the transporter-erector structure, writing: “Next stop integrated hotfire.” The hotfire, another term for the static fire test, was the final major verification step standing between the company and a launch date for NG-4. It never completed. The explosion occurred shortly before 9 p.m. EDT at Space Launch Complex 36, and the last time a rocket exploded on a pad at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station was September 2016, when a helium tank rupture destroyed a SpaceX Falcon 9 at Space Launch Complex 40, roughly two miles north of where New Glenn stood Thursday night.
Jeff Bezos wrote on X that everyone was safe and that it was too early to know the root cause, but that the company was already working to find it, adding they would rebuild whatever needed rebuilding and get back to flying. NASA administrator Jared Isaacman confirmed the agency was aware of the anomaly at Launch Complex 36 and stated it would work with partners to investigate, assess near-term mission impacts, and resume launches, including providing updates on any effects to the Artemis and Moon Base programmes. Elon Musk, whose company SpaceX operates the Falcon 9 and has dominated commercial launch for more than a decade, posted: “Most unfortunate. Rockets are hard.” SpaceX’s position in the market, already commanding, tightened further Thursday night, because Blue Origin had been the only company with a rocket in the same payload class actively competing in the United States.
This is my video of the explosion of the Blue Origin New Glenn rocket at Cape Canaveral’s pad LC-36 a short time ago. Includes video & audio from roughly 5 miles away near Jetty Park. That was an absolutely enormous explosion! 🤯
Note: Thankfully, Blue says all staff are OK. pic.twitter.com/YePg5OmXd8
— JohnCn (@JConcilus) May 29, 2026
New Glenn made its first flight in January 2025, reaching orbit on that debut mission, though the booster exploded before Blue Origin could land it on a drone ship at sea; investigators later attributed that failure to engines that did not properly reignite during the descent burn. The second flight, in November 2025, carried twin NASA ESCAPADE spacecraft toward Mars and successfully landed the booster for the first time. That same booster flew again on the third mission in April 2026, landing a second time on a company barge at sea before the upper stage failure lost the satellite. New Glenn’s first stage, powered by seven BE-6 engines, had in fact performed without serious fault across all three missions, stunning competitors with back-to-back booster recoveries; it was the upper stage that cost the company its payload on mission three, and it is the entire vehicle that the company has now lost on the pad before mission four.
The scale of the setback runs beyond a single destroyed rocket. Blue Origin’s entire commercial strategy hinges on New Glenn as the launch backbone for Amazon’s Leo network, a constellation requiring dozens of launches over several years to become operational. The destruction of a fully assembled rocket on the pad, before its fourth-ever flight, raises a direct question about how far behind schedule the Leo network now sits, given that Amazon had publicly committed to Blue Origin as its primary launch provider just 24 hours before the explosion. The FAA confirmed it was aware of the failure but noted the static fire test was not within the scope of FAA-licensed activities, referring further questions to the company. Congressman Mike Haridopolos, who represents the Florida district that is home to Cape Canaveral, confirmed he had spoken with NASA administrator Isaacman about the incident Thursday night.
As of Friday 29 May 2026, Launch Complex 36 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station remains closed. The lightning protection tower collapse and the blast damage to surrounding structures mean the pad itself faces a rebuilding timeline that is independent of, and likely longer than, whatever investigation into the root cause of the explosion now requires. LC-36 is currently Blue Origin’s only orbital launch facility. No return-to-flight estimate, damage assessment, or cause determination had been issued as of early Friday morning.

sources.news_title: Bezos’ Blue Origin Rocket Explodes On Launch Pad Engine Test
sources.text:
Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin space company suffered a major setback on Thursday night when its New Glenn rocket exploded in a massive fireball on a launch pad at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida U.S. during a routine engine-firing test.
The explosion occurred around 9pm local time as engineers were counting down to a brief test firing of the New Glenn’s seven methane-fuelled BE-4 first stage engines, with the 188-foot-tall first stage becoming enveloped in a rapidly growing fire before the 86-foot-tall upper stage tilted and began to fall.
The rocket was destroyed entirely and as the smoke cleared, the erector-gantry used to move the New Glenn from its hangar to the pad was no longer visible, with one of two tall lightning towers also apparently destroyed and multiple fires burning across the severely damaged pad.
No one was hurt. “All personnel are accounted for and safe. It’s too early to know the root cause but we’re already working to find it. Very rough day, but we’ll rebuild whatever needs rebuilding and get back to flying. Rockets are hard,” Bezos said in a post on X.
Blue Origin had been preparing the New Glenn for its fourth launch, which was slated to deploy a batch of satellites for Amazon’s Leo constellation, a rival internet satellite network to Elon Musk’s SpaceX Starlink, with none of the satellites on board at the time of the explosion.
Just two days before the explosion, NASA had awarded Blue Origin a contract to launch the first of three missions to begin construction of a Moon Base on the lunar surface, due to take place later in 2026, as part of the agency’s Artemis programme to return American astronauts to the Moon in 2028.
NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said the agency was aware of the incident and would provide information on any impacts to the Artemis and Moon Base programmes as it became available, saying “spaceflight is unforgiving, and developing new heavy-lift launch capability is extraordinarily difficult.”
The New Glenn had already been grounded in April after it left a satellite in the wrong orbit because of an engine failure, making Thursday’s explosion the second major setback for the rocket within two months and raising serious questions about Blue Origin’s ability to keep pace with SpaceX in the rapidly growing commercial space industry.

sources.news_title: Blue Origin rocket explodes on launchpad in setback to catch SpaceX
sources.text:
An uncrewed Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded on a Florida launchpad during a test on Thursday in a major setback for Jeff Bezos’s space venture as it seeks to narrow the gap with Elon Musk’s IPO-bound SpaceX.
Video posted by Nasa Spaceflight, which livestreams launches from Florida, showed the towering New Glenn rocket igniting on the pad early on Friday before erupting into a massive fireball that billowed skyward, sending a towering plume of flames and smoke into the air.
Blue Origin was preparing the rocket for its fourth launch, which was due to deliver 48 Amazon Leo satellites into low-Earth orbit, part of efforts to build a broadband constellation to rival Musk’s Starlink network. Amazon Leo satellites were not integrated on the rocket at the time of the incident, a source familiar with the matter said, asking not to be named due to its sensitivity.
The explosion marks the latest setback for the long-delayed New Glenn, which is supposed to play a central role in delivering lunar landers and cargo under Nasa’s Artemis lunar exploration missions.
It comes two days after Nasa awarded Blue Origin a $188m (R3bn) contract to land rovers on the moon’s surface, and less than a week after SpaceX, years ahead in development, carried out a largely successful test of its next-generation Starship rocket.
Blue Origin confirmed it had experienced an “anomaly” during a hot-fire test, where a rocket engine is fired up while anchored to the ground.
“Very rough day, but we’ll rebuild whatever needs rebuilding and get back to flying. It’s worth it,” Bezos said in a post on X, adding it was too early to know the root cause.
Nasa administrator Jared Isaacman said the agency would work with Blue Origin to support an investigation of the incident.
“Spaceflight is unforgiving, and developing new heavy-lift launch capability is extraordinarily difficult,” Isaacman said on X.
He said Nasa would provide information on any impacts to its Artemis and Moon Base programmes.
‘Rockets are hard’
Musk’s SpaceX and Bezos’s Blue Origin, in the latest competition between the billionaire-run companies, have been racing to help return people to the moon ahead of a planned crewed mission by China in 2030 by designing the lunar landers Nasa will use.
SpaceX, which unveiled its plans for an IPO earlier this month and is set to become the first $1-trillion US market debut, has also faced setbacks with its rockets.
In June last year, its massive Starship spacecraft exploded in a similarly dramatic fireball during testing in Texas while preparing for a test flight.
SpaceX was partly successful in its 12th test flight of a Starship prototype last week after it deployed a clutch of mock satellites and executed a controlled splashdown of the spacecraft in the Indian Ocean. But the Musk-owned company failed to achieve a controlled landing of the Super Heavy booster, which tumbled into the Gulf of Mexico.
Musk responded on X to a video of the Blue Origin explosion, saying: “Most unfortunate. Rockets are hard.”
Blue Origin has spent billions and about a decade developing New Glenn, a rocket 29-storeys high with a reusable first stage meant to compete with SpaceX’s Falcon fleet and its more powerful Starship.
The US Federal Aviation Administration said it was aware of the incident, but added it was outside its scope and did not affect air traffic in the region.

sources.news_title: Blue Origin rocket explodes in Florida during launch pad test
sources.text:
WATCH: Blue Origin rocket explodes in Florida during launch pad test
Blue Origin had itself a brutal night in Florida.
A New Glenn rocket exploded Thursday night at Cape Canaveral during a hot-fire test, sending a massive fireball into the sky and leaving officials warning boaters about debris in the water along Florida’s Space Coast.
Nobody was hurt, which is the only part of this story that actually matters from a human standpoint. But from a space race standpoint, this was a disaster.
>> Shop Philly Sports Gear Here
The rocket was supposed to stay anchored to the ground while its engines fired. That is the whole point of a hot-fire test. Instead, the thing went up in flames around 9 p.m. and turned the launch pad into a scene from a movie where the billionaire tech project finally meets reality.
Blue Origin called it an “anomaly.”
That is the space industry’s favorite word for “the rocket exploded.”
Jeff Bezos called it a “very rough day” and said the company would rebuild what needs rebuilding. He also said it is too early to know what caused it. Fair enough. You probably need more than a few hours to figure out why your 300-foot-plus rocket just became a fireball in front of everyone.
Blue Origin Has Bigger Problems Than One Explosion
This is not just one bad test.
Blue Origin is trying to make New Glenn a real player in the heavy-lift launch market. That means competing with SpaceX, carrying commercial satellites, handling government work, and proving it can be trusted with major NASA missions.
That becomes a little harder when the rocket explodes on the pad.
>> Read More Trending Stories Here
The timing makes it worse. New Glenn already had issues earlier this year when a launch left a commercial satellite in the wrong orbit. The FAA had to get involved. Blue Origin blamed that one on an engine problem.
Now this happens.
So the company goes from trying to build momentum to explaining another failure. That is a tough spot, especially when the whole sales pitch is built around reliability, reusability, and being ready for the next phase of commercial spaceflight.
The Debris Warning Tells You How Serious This Was
After the explosion, the U.S. Coast Guard warned boaters about debris in the water near a restricted section of the coast. Mariners were told to avoid the area because of debris hazards and ongoing launch and recovery operations.
That detail makes the whole thing feel a lot less abstract.
This was not just some controlled test that went wrong inside a lab. This was a rocket exploding on Florida’s Space Coast, debris becoming a water hazard, and officials having to tell people to stay away.
Again, thankfully, nobody was hurt. But that does not make it minor.
Bezos Can Say They Will Rebuild, But This Is A Setback
To Bezos’ credit, he did not pretend this was nothing. He called it a rough day and said Blue Origin would keep going.
That is probably the only answer he can give.
Space is hard. Rockets fail. Tests go wrong. Every company in this industry has blown something up at some point. SpaceX has had plenty of public failures too. The difference is SpaceX has also stacked enough wins to make the failures feel like part of the process.
Blue Origin is still trying to prove it belongs in that conversation.
That is why this explosion hits harder. New Glenn is not some side project. It is the rocket Blue Origin needs if it wants to be taken seriously beyond space tourism and celebrity flights.
NASA is involved. Amazon satellite plans are involved. The commercial launch market is involved. The Artemis program is involved.
So yes, Blue Origin can rebuild. It probably will.
But last night in Florida was not just a bad visual. It was a reminder that Blue Origin is still chasing the version of itself it keeps promising everyone it will become.

Jeff Bezos just had a very bad night in Florida. The company confirmed no personnel were injured, calling the incident an “anomaly” while promising updates as the investigation unfolds.
The explosion is the latest in a string of setbacks for Bezos’ aerospace company. The New Glenn rocket had already been grounded earlier this year after the FAA required Blue Origin to investigate a separate engine incident. Thursday’s fireball will almost certainly trigger yet another federal review, further delaying a program that has faced repeated scrutiny.
The timing is particularly brutal. Just days before the explosion, NASA announced it had selected Blue Origin over Elon Musk’s SpaceX to lead the first of three uncrewed lunar missions this year, part of a $20 billion moon base construction initiative.
Both companies are also locked in competition to provide crew landers for the Artemis program, including the planned 2028 return of astronauts to the lunar surface.
Musk, never one to stay quiet, offered a characteristically loaded response on X. “Most unfortunate,” he wrote. “Rockets are hard.” Coming from a man whose own company won the contract Blue Origin is racing to catch up to, the sympathy rang hollow.

New Glenn rocket lost in explosion
May 29, 2026
By Chris Forrester
A Blue Origin rocket, named New Glenn #4, was lost during a static test firing of its engines while standing at Launch Complex 36 at the Kennedy Space Center. Amazon founder Jeff Bezos backs the Blue Origin projects. The explosion happened at about 9pm Florida time (01.00 UTC) on May 28th.
The loss of the NG-4 rocket is a notable set-back for the launch company. It will also mean a major reconstruction of the launch pad and associated ground support equipment which might take as long as 12 or more months to repair/rebuild. LC-36 appears to have suffered significant damage, with several towers and other structures entirely missing,
It is also a set-back for AST SpaceMobile which had expected the rocket to launch a batch of its satellites next week. AST’s share price tumbled 7 percent ($9.37) in after-market trading on May 28th.
A message from Bezos said: “All personnel are accounted for and safe. It’s too early to know the root cause but we’re already working to find it. Very rough day, but we’ll rebuild whatever needs rebuilding and get back to flying. It’s worth it”.
Also likely to suffer significant consequences will be the Amazon-backed Leo satellite constellation which was depending on New Glenn to launch its fleet.
Blue Origin, in a statement after the explosion, said: “We experienced an anomaly during today’s hot-fire test. All personnel have been accounted for. We will provide updates as we learn more.”
Elon Musk, despite being a fierce competitor and allegedly no friend of Bezos, said on his X social media platform: “Sorry to see this, I hope you recover quickly.”
The consequences for AST are significant. There are suggestions that AST’s commercial launch will now slip into very late 2027 or 2028. sources.news_title: New Glenn rocket explodes on launch pad during test
sources.text:
Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket exploded today during a hotfire test on its launch pad in Florida — dealing heavy damage to the pad, and dealing a heavy blow to Jeff Bezos’ space venture.
“All personnel are accounted for and safe,” Bezos said in a post to X. “It’s too early to know the root cause but we’re already working to find it. Very rough day, but we’ll rebuild whatever needs rebuilding and get back to flying. It’s worth it.”
The U.S. Space Force confirmed that there were no injuries or fatalities. “Range officials, in coordination with Blue Origin and appropriate partners, are currently evaluating available data to determine the exact cause of the anomaly,” it said in a Facebook post. In a follow-up post to X, the Space Force’s Space Launch Delta 45 cautioned that debris from the anomaly could wash ashore over the coming days or weeks.
The 322-foot-tall rocket, nicknamed “No, It’s Necessary” in a reference to the movie “Interstellar,” had been due to send 48 Amazon Leo satellites into orbit as soon as next week. The Federal Aviation Administration gave its go-ahead for launch last week after Blue Origin wrapped up an investigation of a launch failure that occurred in April.
In preparation for liftoff, the New Glenn rocket was brought out to Blue Origin’s pad at Space Launch Complex 36 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station for a static test firing of its booster engines. The satellites were not aboard the rocket for the test.
Video showed the rocket exploding in a huge fireball after the engines were lit up. “They just nuked the pad,” one observer could be heard saying in a video recorded by Spaceflight Now. Other views of the blast were captured by NASASpaceflight.com.

sources.news_title: Why did Blue Origin’s New Glenn explode?
sources.text:
Why did Blue Origin’s New Glenn explode?
Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket experienced a serious failure during testing in Florida, exploding on or near the launch pad during a ground “hotfire” type engine test. Company statements attributed the event to an “anomaly,” and said that no injuries occurred.
Multiple reports described setbacks occurring either during engine-firing tests or shortly after an engine test phase, with the explosion sending a large fireball and shaking nearby areas. After the incident, Blue Origin said all personnel were accounted for and indicated it would investigate and rebuild as needed.
Why it matters
The explosion is significant because New Glenn is Blue Origin’s planned heavy-lift launcher intended to compete for a major share of the commercial space market. When rockets fail during testing, it can push back schedules for future launches and satellite or government payload missions that depend on the vehicle.
For the U.S. space economy, these kinds of test setbacks can also ripple into contracts and timelines for customers who are counting on dependable launch capacity. In addition, frequent disruptions can affect investor confidence in the company’s execution.
The broader context is that competition among launch providers is central to reducing launch costs and increasing delivery reliability. A major failure can therefore influence procurement decisions by agencies and commercial firms evaluating which systems to trust for near-term needs.
Bottom line
Blue Origin reported the New Glenn explosion happened after an engine test anomaly during a Florida test campaign, with the company emphasizing personnel were safe and that it would investigate. The incident matters because it can affect New Glenn’s timetable and the reliability of U.S. launch capacity.

sources.news_title: Blue Origin Rocket Blows Up During Testing—Bezos And Musk Comment
sources.text:
Topline
Blue Origin’s new rocket exploded on the launchpad in Florida during a test that was being conducted to prepare for an upcoming launch, dealing a major blow to the Jeff Bezos-backed rocket company and its bid to challenge Elon Musk’s SpaceX.
Key Facts
In a statement on X, Blue Origin said it experienced an “anomaly” during a “hotfire test” of its New Glenn rocket—a process where a rocket’s engines are ignited while it remains bolted to the launch pad.
Videos of the incident showed flames rising from beneath the rocket and rising upwards during the test fire, before everything exploded into a large fireball.
The company didn’t provide any details about the “anomaly” that caused the explosion, but noted that all “personnel have been accounted for.
According to the New York Times, the explosion damaged Blue Origin’s sole launchpad for the New Glenn rocket at the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station and repairs are likely to take several months.
The New Glenn rocket was being prepared to launch 48 Amazon Leo satellites into low Earth orbit as the Starlink competitor attempts to grow its satellite internet offering.
Crucial Quote
Billionaire and Blue Origin founder Jeff Bezos commented on the incident in a X post, saying: “All personnel are accounted for and safe. It’s too early to know the root cause, but we’re already working to find it. Very rough day, but we’ll rebuild whatever needs rebuilding and get back to flying. It’s worth it.”
Tangent
Responding to Blue Origin’s announcement on X, SpaceX CEO Elon Musk wrote: “Sorry to see this, I hope you recover quickly.”
What Has Nasa Said About The Incident?
NASA administrator Jared Isaacman wrote the government space agency is “aware of the anomaly” involving the Blue Origin New Glenn test. “Spaceflight is unforgiving, and developing new heavy-lift launch capability is extraordinarily difficult. We will work with our partners to support a thorough investigation of this anomaly, assess near-term mission impacts, and get back to launching rockets.” The statement also added that NASA will share updates on any potential impacts to the Artemis and Moon Base programs “as it becomes available.”

sources.news_title: Bezos rocket erupts in fireball during ground test
sources.text:
An uncrewed Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded on the launchpad during a test on Thursday, in a major setback for Jeff Bezos’s space venture as it seeks to narrow the gap with Elon Musk’s soon-to-be-listed SpaceX.
Video posted by NasaSpaceflight, a YouTube channel that livestreams launches from Florida, showed the New Glenn igniting on the pad at about 3am SAST (9pm local time) before erupting into a massive fireball that billowed skyward, sending a towering plume of flames and smoke into the air.
Blue Origin said it had experienced an “anomaly”, a term commonly used by rocket companies to describe a launch failure or explosion.
“We experienced an anomaly during today’s hotfire test. All personnel have been accounted for. We will provide updates as we learn more,” the company said in a post on X. A hot-fire test is where a rocket engine is fired up while anchored to the ground.
Nasa administrator Jared Isaacman said the agency was aware of the incident.
“Spaceflight is unforgiving, and developing new heavy-lift launch capability is extraordinarily difficult. We will work with our partners to support a thorough investigation of this anomaly, assess near-term mission impacts and get back to launching rockets,” he said on X.
Isaacman also added that Nasa would provide information on any impacts to its Artemis and Moon Base programmes.
‘Very rough day’
Earlier this week, Nasa awarded Blue Origin a US$188-million contract to deliver rovers to the moon’s surface using its uncrewed cargo lunar lander, Mark 1, as part of Nasa’s broader Artemis lunar exploration missions.
In a separate X post, Bezos said it was “too early to know the root cause” of the incident. “Very rough day, but we’ll rebuild whatever needs rebuilding and get back to flying. It’s worth it.”
Musk’s SpaceX and Bezos’s Blue Origin, in the latest competition between the billionaire-run companies, have been racing to help return people to the moon ahead of a planned crewed mission by China in 2030 by designing the lunar landers Nasa will use.
Read: Blue Origin reaches orbit in challenge to SpaceX
SpaceX, which unveiled its plans for an IPO earlier this month and is set to become the first trillion-dollar US market debut, has also faced setbacks.
In June last year, its massive Starship spacecraft exploded in a similarly dramatic fireball during testing in Texas while preparing for a test flight.
SpaceX was partly successful in its 12th test flight of a Starship prototype last week after it deployed a clutch of mock satellites and executed a controlled splashdown of the spacecraft in the Indian Ocean. But the Musk-owned company failed to achieve a controlled landing of the Super Heavy booster, which tumbled into the Gulf of Mexico.
Musk responded on X to a video of the Blue Origin explosion, saying: “Most unfortunate. Rockets are hard.”
Blue Origin had said on Wednesday it was preparing the New Glenn rocket to launch 48 Amazon Leo satellites into low-Earth orbit, part of efforts to build a broadband constellation to rival Musk’s Starlink network. It did not provide a launch date.
Read: SpaceX wants to fly a rocket every 53 minutes
The company has spent billions of dollars and roughly a decade developing New Glenn, a rocket 29-storeys high with a reusable first stage meant to compete with SpaceX’s Falcon fleet and its more powerful Starship.
The US Federal Aviation Administration said it was aware of the incident, but added that it was outside its scope and did not impact air traffic in the region. — Gnaneshwar Rajan and Joe Brock, with David Shepardson, (c) 2026 Reuters

sources.news_title: Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin suffers massive New Glenn rocket explosion ahead of key satellite mission
sources.text:
Jeff Bezos’ Blue Origin suffers massive New Glenn rocket explosion ahead of key satellite mission
Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket exploded during a static fire test at Cape Canaveral, Florida, in a major setback for Jeff Bezos’ space company. The rocket was being prepared for its fourth mission when the blast occurred, prompting an investigation and likely delaying future launches.
New Delhi: Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket suffered a major explosion during a ground test at Cape Canaveral, Florida, on Thursday, dealing a significant setback to Jeff Bezos’ space company ahead of its planned fourth mission. It was a routine static fire test, which is performed before a rocket can be launched, as it was readied for its next mission with Amazon’s Project Kuiper internet satellites.
Later the company admitted that an “anomaly” had taken place during testing and that all personnel were safe. Jeff Bezos also said that everyone had been accounted for. The cause of the failure is still being investigated, but the incident is likely to result in an extended investigation and potentially a postponement of Blue Origin’s launch schedule for several months.
Massive explosion during pre-launch testing
Here’s our video of the explosion at Launch Complex 36. It happened about 9 pm ET (0100 UTC) as Blue Origin was beginning a static fire test of its New Glenn rocket. Watch live views: https://t.co/tm2wZQmAVD pic.twitter.com/PmbgQC6Qmq — Spaceflight Now (@SpaceflightNow) May 29, 2026New Glenn was undergoing a static fire test at Blue Origin’s launch facility in Cape Canaveral when the explosion occurred. When such tests are conducted, rocket engines are fired in a vehicle that is still bound to the launch pad. The footage filmed by NASASpaceFlight.com and Spaceflight Now showed the rocket exploding into a huge fireball during the process. This test was probably a full-dress affair, since New Glenn was already full of fuel, and it was one of the most important rocket blasts ever witnessed in the United States in recent years. Blue Origin confirmed the incident in a statement on X without revealing any details of what might have caused the failure.
Bezos vows recovery effort
Shortly after the incident, Bezos admitted that the setback was a matter of concern and that the company has started investigating the cause of the setback.
Bezos said in a post on X that while it’s too soon to determine the cause, they’re already getting to work on uncovering it. It was a pretty rough day but we’ll fix what needs fixing and we’ll get back to flying.”
His remarks reiterate Blue Origin’s approach to the development of New Glenn in the wake of a significant loss.
NASA and FAA monitoring situation
The explosion has attracted the interest of the U.S. space program-related federal agencies.
NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said the agency would investigate in detail and look at any impact on future missions. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) also acknowledged it heard of the incident, and that air traffic was not disrupted.
Several of NASA’s future programs rely on Blue Origin, which makes the results of this investigation quite significant, such as the study’s relevance to the Artemis moon exploration program.
New Glenn faces another setback
The explosion follows New Glenn’s third rocket launch in orbit, which recently had issues with one of its engines. In that mission, the upper stage in the rocket experienced a failure of the cryogenic system, which meant that a satellite built by AST failed to reach its planned orbit.
Blue Origin’s investigation into that mission has been completed and the FAA had recently authorized New Glenn to return to flight. Now the question is about the rocket’s near future with the explosion on Thursday.
Blue Origin had hoped to conduct up to 12 New Glenn launches this year as it ramps up competition with SpaceX in the commercial launch market.
A decade-long development journey
New Glenn is the product of almost 10 years of development at Blue Origin. In January 2025, the heavy-lift rocket successfully entered orbit, which was a significant achievement for the company.
Its second flight in November 2025, with NASA spacecraft onboard and the first successful booster landing, was seen as even more successful. The company then recycled the booster for the third flight of New Glenn, showcasing an important function that can help to reduce the cost of launching rockets.
Those successes pale in comparison to what happened Thursday, which marks the biggest screw-up in New Glenn history.
Impact on Amazon’s satellite ambitions
The failed test was tied to the preparations for New Glenn’s fourth mission, which would be for Amazon’s Project Kuiper satellite internet network. Amazon has signed up 24 New Glenn missions with Blue Origin to launch its rival to SpaceX’s Starlink satellite broadband service.
Amazon later wrote that no Kuiper satellites were on-board when the rocket tested, and thus no valuable payloads were lost.
However, the delay may have an impact on the company’s efforts to quickly build out its satellite constellation in the next few years.
Industry reaction
The incident sparked a response from all the space industry, including from SpaceX CEO Elon Musk.
“Most unfortunate. Rockets are hard,” Musk wrote on X. “I hope you recover quickly.”
Local authorities were also relieved that no injuries were reported. Congressman Mike Haridopolos, who represents Cape Canaveral, said he had contacted NASA officials after the explosion and expressed his gratitude to first responders and the launch teams’ speedy response.
Now Blue Origin has one big hurdle to clear out of the way as it seeks to bounce back from a major disappointment in its bid to become a major player in the launch industry.

A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket has dramatically exploded on the launchpad during a test in a setback for Jeff Bezos’ space venture as it seeks to narrow the gap with Elon Musk’s SpaceX.
Video posted by NasaSpaceflight, a YouTube channel that livestreams launches from Florida, showed the New Glenn igniting on the pad at about 9pm Eastern Time on Thursday, or 10am Hong Kong time on Friday, before erupting into a massive fireball that billowed skywards, sending a towering plume of flames and smoke into the air.
Blue Origin said it had experienced an “anomaly”, a term commonly used by rocket companies to describe a launch failure or explosion.
“We experienced an anomaly during today’s hotfire test. All personnel have been accounted for. We will provide updates as we learn more,” the company said in a post on X.
A hotfire test is where a rocket engine is fired up while anchored to the ground.
In a separate X post, Bezos said it was "too early to know the root cause" of the incident.
"Very rough day, but we’ll rebuild whatever needs rebuilding and get back to flying. It’s worth it," he said.
Blue Origin said on Wednesday it was preparing the New Glenn rocket to launch 48 Amazon Leo satellites into low-Earth orbit, part of efforts to build a broadband constellation to rival Musk’s Starlink network. It did not provide a launch date.
Blue Origin has spent billions of dollars and roughly a decade developing New Glenn, a rocket 29-stories high with a reusable first stage meant to compete with SpaceX's Falcon fleet and its more powerful Starship.
Musk responded on X to a video of the New Glenn explosion, saying: “Most unfortunate. Rockets are hard.” (Reuters)
Edited by Thomas McAlinden

sources.news_title: New Glenn rocket explodes on launch pad
sources.text:
Blue Origin's space ambitions have suffered a major setback as its New Glenn rocket exploded in a fireball on the launch pad at about 7:00 pm EDT at Launch Complex 36 (LC-36), Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida during an engine test.
According to Blue Origin and news reports, the explosion occurred while the fully stacked vehicle was undergoing a routine hot-fire test that involved fueling the rocket and a brief ignition of the first-stage liquid methane/oxygen engines ahead of the scheduled NG-4 orbital mission.
Details of the incident are still emerging, but Blue Origin founder Jeff Bezos has confirmed that there were no casualties.
"All personnel are accounted for and safe," said Bezos in a post on X. "It’s too early to know the root cause but we’re already working to find it. Very rough day, but we’ll rebuild whatever needs rebuilding and get back to flying. It’s worth it."
Blue Origin's New Glenn just blew up at LC-36 while attempting to Static Fire ahead of NG-4.https://t.co/tANS0dWyIH pic.twitter.com/PztxFoBqIw
— NSF - NASASpaceflight.com (@NASASpaceflight) May 29, 2026
Despite this, there have been reports of major infrastructure damage. The rocket appears to have been completely destroyed and one lightning arrestor tower has vanished. It is feared that the pad, hangars, and adjacent test facilities have also been impacted. However, there was no payload atop the rocket at the time of the incident.
New Glenn is a heavy-lift, partially reusable two-stage launch vehicle developed by Blue Origin to support commercial satellite constellations, national security launches, and civil spaceflight programs, including NASA’s Artemis lunar initiative. With the apparent loss of the rocket and possible damage to Blue Origin's only operational New Glenn launch complex, future flight schedules are likely to be significantly affected while repairs and investigations are carried out.
Source: Blue Origin

A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded Thursday in Brevard County, Florida, filling the night sky with fire along Florida’s Space Coast.
Video below: Blue Origin explosion rocks Florida’s Space Coast
A spokesperson for the U.S. Space Force confirmed the rocket exploded at 9 p.m. at Space Launch Complex 36 during a hotfire test, which Blue Origin itself described earlier on social media.
“We experienced an anomaly during today’s hotfire test,” Blue Origin’s post states. “All personnel have been accounted for. We will provide updates as we learn more.”
The Brevard County Sheriff’s Office said in a statement it had received info “that there was a failure of the test firing and an explosion,” adding preliminary reports show no injuries.
Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket was recently transported to Launch Complex 36 at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station ahead of the planned Leo New Glenn 1 launch.
Congressman Mike Haridopolos, R-Brevard County, said on social media that he had spoken with NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman and is grateful no injuries were reported.
Rep. Haridopolos is the chairman of the House Science, Space, and Technology Subcommittee on Space and Aeronautics.
Space expert Ken Kremer joined Orlando sister station WESH to discuss the explosion.
“They were loading propellant into the rocket, and they started a static fire test, which is not a launch; the rocket is sitting on the pad, and they want to ignite the engines for several seconds to test them all out and make sure everything will work when they do the launch in the next few weeks. That was the plan,” he said.
Both SpaceX and United Launch Alliance are scheduled to launch Falcon 9 and Atlas V rockets, respectively, from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station on Friday.

sources.news_title: Blue Origin Rocket Explodes During Florida Launch Test
sources.text:
A massive explosion rocked Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida after a Blue Origin New Glenn rocket suffered what the company described as an “anomaly” during a hotfire test on the launch pad.
The dramatic blast occurred at around 9 p.m. Eastern Time on Thursday, May 28, at Launch Complex 36, sending a towering fireball and mushroom cloud into the sky as shockwaves reportedly rippled across parts of central Florida.
Blue Origin later confirmed the incident in a statement posted on social media, saying all personnel had been safely accounted for.
“We experienced an anomaly during today’s hotfire test,” the company said. “All personnel have been accounted for. We will provide updates as we learn more.”
New Glenn rocket program
The company had been preparing the massive New Glenn rocket for a planned static-fire engine test ahead of its anticipated fourth mission, which was expected to launch as early as June 4 carrying 48 satellites for Amazon’s Kuiper internet constellation.
Also Read: Dallas Explosion Devastates Apartment Building — 11 Feared Trapped in Rubble
The satellite project is viewed as a direct competitor to Elon Musk’s Starlink network operated by SpaceX.
Authorities said there was no immediate threat to the public despite the scale of the explosion.
Brevard County Emergency Management said emergency crews were monitoring the situation while allowing the contained fire to burn itself out naturally.
“The current plan is to allow the contained fire caused by the explosion to burn itself out,” local emergency officials said in a statement.
The City of Cape Canaveral also confirmed that its Emergency Operations Team had been placed in active contact with Canaveral Fire Rescue following the incident.
“An explosion occurred on the pad,” the city said. “According to Blue Origin, all personnel have been accounted for.”
The exact cause of the explosion remains under investigation.
Eyewitnesses described seeing an enormous flash followed by a loud blast that could be felt miles away from the launch site.
“I was walking my dog and saw a giant flash of orange from East Orlando,” one witness, Sam Bates, wrote on social media.
Footage circulating online appeared to show severe destruction around the launch complex, including what observers said was the collapse of one of the lightning-protection towers near the launch pad.
Setback for Blue Origin
The incident marks a major setback for Blue Origin’s ambitious New Glenn rocket program, which has been under development for nearly a decade as Jeff Bezos seeks to challenge SpaceX’s dominance in the commercial launch industry.
Named after legendary astronaut John Glenn, the New Glenn rocket stands approximately 322 feet tall and is designed as a reusable heavy-lift launch vehicle capable of carrying satellites, spacecraft, and future deep-space missions.
The rocket’s reusable first stage is powered by seven BE-4 engines fueled by liquid oxygen and liquid methane, generating more than 3.8 million pounds of thrust at liftoff.
Blue Origin has promoted New Glenn as a major competitor to SpaceX’s Falcon Heavy and Starship systems.
Despite years of delays, the rocket had recently begun achieving significant milestones.
New Glenn successfully reached orbit during its first flight in January 2025, although the upper stage later broke apart before a planned drone ship landing attempt.
A second mission in November 2025 successfully delivered a NASA spacecraft to Mars and achieved the program’s first booster landing.
However, the rocket’s third mission suffered another setback after an upper-stage malfunction prevented an AST SpaceMobile satellite from reaching its intended orbit.
Thursday night’s explosion now threatens to delay Blue Origin’s broader commercial ambitions, including Amazon’s Project Kuiper deployment schedule.
Also Read: UK Deploys New Anti-Drone Missile System to Middle East Amid Hormuz Security Build-up
Project Kuiper is a major Amazon initiative designed to create a global broadband internet network using thousands of satellites in low Earth orbit — directly competing with Musk’s Starlink system, which already operates across dozens of countries.
Elon Musk reacts
The rivalry between Bezos and Musk has increasingly expanded beyond business into the aerospace sector, where SpaceX currently dominates launch services, reusable rocket operations and satellite internet deployment.
Musk reacted publicly to the explosion shortly after reports emerged online.
“Most unfortunate. Rockets are hard,” the SpaceX founder wrote on X.
He later added another message directly responding to Blue Origin’s official statement: “Sorry to see this, I hope you recover quickly.”
The response drew attention online given the intense commercial rivalry between the two billionaire-led companies.
The failed test comes during a period of heightened competition in the global space industry as private companies race to secure military contracts, satellite launches, lunar missions and future deep-space exploration opportunities.
Investigators are now expected to assess what triggered the catastrophic failure during the ground test and whether the incident caused significant long-term damage to the infrastructure at Launch Complex 36.
Blue Origin has not yet indicated whether the planned June launch timeline for the next New Glenn mission will be affected.

sources.news_title: Blue Origin’s New Glenn Rocket Explodes During Static Fire Test at Cape Canaveral
sources.text:
Blue Origin’s New Glenn rocket suffered a dramatic failure late Thursday night when it exploded in a massive fireball during a planned static fire test at Launch Complex 36 in Cape Canaveral, Florida.
The incident unfolded as crews prepared the first-stage booster for the rocket’s upcoming NG-4 mission, which was expected to deploy 48 Amazon Project Kuiper internet satellites into orbit in early June. Video from the scene captured the rocket’s seven BE-4 engines igniting briefly before a violent detonation sent flames and debris shooting skyward, lighting up the night with an intense orange glow visible from as far as 50 miles away in Orlando.
No injuries were reported, though the blast is believed to have inflicted significant damage on both the rocket hardware and the launch pad infrastructure. Blue Origin has not yet issued a detailed statement on the cause, but an investigation is anticipated, likely involving the Federal Aviation Administration as it reviews the commercial space test.
New Glenn, the heavy-lift vehicle developed by Jeff Bezos’ company, has logged three successful flights since January 2025, including missions that delivered payloads and demonstrated booster reuse. Those achievements positioned the rocket as a credible competitor in the growing commercial launch market, particularly for large satellite constellations like Amazon’s Kuiper network.
This latest setback underscores the unforgiving nature of rocket engineering, even for a program that has made steady progress in recent months. While the company’s prior tests and launches had built momentum, ground testing remains a critical—and risky—step before committing hardware to flight.
Observers noted the stark contrast with the rapid cadence now common at other commercial providers, where such anomalies draw immediate scrutiny amid intense competition for government and private contracts. Blue Origin will now face the task of analyzing data from the failed test, repairing or replacing affected components, and determining how this delay impacts its schedule for Kuiper and other payloads.
For now, the focus remains on safety protocols and root-cause analysis, standard procedure following any anomaly of this scale. The explosion serves as a reminder that reaching orbit consistently demands precision at every stage, from the pad to the pad’s edge.

sources.text:
Blue Origin rocket explodes in 'anomaly' at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station
Video captures Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket exploding into a huge plume of flames at Launch Complex 36 around 9 p.m.
CAPE CANAVERAL, Flo. - A Blue Origin rocket exploded during a static fire test at the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station late Thursday night.
Video captures Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket exploding into a huge plume of flames at Launch Complex 36 around 9 p.m.
NASA SHIFTS FROM VISITING THE MOON TO BUILDING ON IT
"I was standing outside, and the night sky completely lit up, and we all heard the boom," Cape Canaveral Mayor Wes Morrison said on Facebook.
NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said NASA is aware of the incident, and no injuries have been reported. All personnel are accounted for and safe, officials said.
"It’s too early to know the root cause, but we’re already working to find it," Jeff Bezos, who founded Blue Origin, said on social media.
Officials called the incident an "anomaly" and said Blue Origin will "rebuild whatever needs rebuilding and get back flying."
Space Launch Delta 45, which oversees the Eastern Range at Cape Canaveral Space Force Station and Kennedy Space Center, said the incident occurred during a hot-fire test of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket.
They said the Eastern Range remains fully mission capable for National Security Space Launch and continues to support operations at all other launch complexes.
CRYSTAL BALL NEBULA SEEN IN STUNNING NEW SPACE IMAGE 1,500 LIGHT-YEARS AWAY
"The Eastern Range serves as a Department of War test and training range supporting critical development, testing, evaluation and launch activities that advance national security and space capabilities. These operations often involve developmental systems and emerging technologies, and the nature of such testing carries inherent risk, including the potential for anomalies," Space Launch Delta 45 said in a statement.
Space Launch Delta 45 said debris from the explosion could wash ashore along publicly accessible areas in the coming days and weeks. Anyone who sees this debris should call 911.
Launch vehicle debris is potentially hazardous, and direct contact poses a risk to personal health and welfare, according to officials.
Isaacman said NASA will provide information on any impacts on the Artemis and Moon Base programs as it becomes available.
NASA’S PERSEVERANCE ROVER CAPTURES STUNNING SELFIE IN ANCIENT MARTIAN TERRAIN
"Spaceflight is unforgiving, and developing new heavy-lift launch capability is extraordinarily difficult. We will work with our partners to support a thorough investigation of this anomaly, assess near-term mission impacts, and get back to launching rockets," Isaacman said on social media.
Our affiliate, FOX 35 News, said emergency management and fire rescue officials are allowing the contained fire caused by the explosion to burn itself out.
On Blue Origin's website, the New Glenn rocket is described as "our giant, reusable rocket built for bigger things."
NASA STARTS PREPARATIONS FOR ARTEMIS III MISSION WITH SPACE LAUNCH SYSTEM ROLLOUT
Blue Origin is an official commercial launch vehicle contracted to fly agency payloads, and it honors NASA history by being named after John Glenn, the first American to orbit Earth, according to the Center for Strategic and International Studies.
